construction_commit_note: efb8191 is the commit carrying candidates/nhs-ae-four-hour-decline/source/build.py with the M-only eligibility rule (24 volume-qualified months at or before M, M qualifies, target month label-only), the maximum-observed publication lag (13 days), and the docstring/PREDICTION_QUESTION corrected to match that rule - the code the v2026.12 rebuild c executed (run from the committed tree at 2026-10-21T18:06:51Z; CSV output byte-identical to the 15:26 build's summary and to v2026.11's CSVs). History kept for provenance: 5f3fe45 carried the v2026.11 build.py (hindsight-selection fix, publication-date instant) that the 15:26 v2026.12 session also executed, but that session's gate report described mid-fix bytes that were never shipped; 48eab83 carried the pre-fix v2026.10 build.py (sha256 cb1d508a...) whose bytes job nhsae-002 executed were bundled earlier (sha256 7ecf2e1e...); that delta was confined to the HTTP fetch path (the client ladder and failure diagnostics added after nhsae-001 measured the publisher CDN serving HTTP 202 with an empty body to datacenter IPs), and nhsae-002 consumed the staged verified source via --source-dir. The v2026.11 and v2026.12 builds fetched the 102 CSVs over HTTP from the coordinator (summary.source.mode http, 114 requests), so the shipped fetch path did run.

source.name: NHS England - A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions, statistical work area (monthly provider-level CSVs)
source.api: per-financial-year sub-pages (2018-19 through 2026-27) each link 12 monthly provider-level CSVs (~30 KB, 21 columns); pre-2018-19 months are XLS-only; the publisher's CDN serves HTTP 202 with an empty body to datacenter IPs (measured 2026-10-21), so reproduction fetches from this package's build use the coordinator-measured URL set
source.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0 (NHS England / Crown copyright; attribution carries through). Derived research dataset - not an NHS England official product.
